title: Strategic Account Commitment Charter and Intake Protocol
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Create a formalized "Strategic Account Commitment Charter" and a standardized intake protocol for customer-driven roadmap asks from top accounts. The charter defines commitment windows, decision heuristics, and escalation SLAs to give Sales and Customer Success predictable signals about what the product organization can commit to and why.

Motivation:
- Multiple ad-hoc escalations from strategic accounts are causing confusion across Product, Eng, and Sales about timelines and scope.
- We need a reproducible decision process that balances commercial commitments with platform economics and reliability.
- This charter will be used during sales negotiations and renewal conversations to set shared expectations and reduce surprise roadmap promises.

Scope:
- Intake form and rubric for prioritizing strategic-account asks.
- Commitment tiers (e.g., Exploratory, Timebound Pilot, Contracted Commitment) with defined windows and deliverable expectations.
- Escalation SLAs and response routing (PM triage, technical lead consult, capacity check).
- Acceptance criteria and telemetry hooks for post-delivery verification.

Out of scope (for this ticket): formal contract/legal wording; SLA enforcement tooling changes (separate Eng initiatives required).
acceptance_criteria: A public-facing intake checklist is published to Sales and Success (Confluence) explaining tiers and expected timelines.
A one-page decision rubric (scorecard) that Product uses to evaluate strategic asks is finalized and signed off by Head of Product and Growth.
Escalation SLAs are documented, including owner for each SLA action and initial routing rules.
Two pilot intake requests from different accounts are processed end-to-end using the new protocol and feedback incorporated.
Telemetry events are defined so Delivery and Success can report on delivery vs. commitment window (link to events in linked_artifacts).
proposed_workflow: Step 1: Sales/Succ submits Intake form (fields: customer ARR, renewal date, ask description, business impact, willingness to fund, POC timeline, compliance constraints).
Step 2: Automated pre-triage by PM tooling (enrich with account signals: ARR, usage, support tickets, past commitments).
Step 3: PM triage meeting within SLA. Assign commitment tier (Exploratory / Pilot / Contracted).
Step 4: If Pilot/Contracted -> schedule Tech-Feasibility sync with Eng (within 5 business days).
Step 5: Product issues a Commitment Note with window and success metrics; Sales can use in contract conversations.
Step 6: Delivery tracked through a dedicated epic; Success/Customer verify acceptance criteria at end of window.
decision_heuristics: Weighted score: Commercial (40%), Strategic Fit (25%), Technical Feasibility (20%), Risk/Operational Cost (15%).
Commercial: includes ARR at risk, potential expansion, willingness to pay for expedited delivery.
Strategic Fit: alignment to OKRs or platform roadmap (explicit mapping to OKR tag required).
Technical Feasibility: quick judgment on whether change is runtime/config/UI and estimated eng points (<=8 points favors shorter commitment window).
Operational cost threshold: features that increase sustained infra cost require C-level signoff or dedicated funding.
SLA_definitions: Initial ack: 24 business hours for all top-account intake submissions.
Triage decision: within 5 business days for Exploratory vs. Pilot/Contracted classification.
Tech feasibility callback: within 10 business days for Pilot/Contracted; if blocked by infra capacity, escalate to Eng Director within 2 business days.
Commitment window examples: Exploratory (4-8 weeks, non-committal), Pilot (8-12 weeks with a success review), Contracted (calendar quarter commitment; target delivery date agreed with GTM).
Fallback policy: if delivery cannot be met, Product must propose a mitigation within 5 business days (alternative timeline, scoped pivot, or funded expedited path).
metrics_to_track: # of intake requests processed per month for Top Accounts
% of commitments delivered within committed window
Net Promoter impact for accounts with commitments vs. without
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-promising during renewals. Mitigation: enforce 'Commitment Note' as required artifact before Sales includes any firm language in contracts.

Risk: Engineering capacity starvation for platform roadmap. Mitigation: require explicit funding or swap-out of roadmap scope for Contracted commitments; route high-operational-cost work to a special funded backlog.
Risk: Ambiguous success criteria. Mitigation: intake must include measurable acceptance criteria; Product will not sign commitment without them.
